deep.reconstruction:
The page is a narrow paper strip (folio 27v) of scratch algebra with no prose, so the purpose is not stated and my reading is tentative. Context from the neighbouring pages: the previous page tabulates, for Gaussian primes P and a modulus p = 1+2i, counts k^0..k''' of residues falling in each biquadratic residue class, together with a short list of values of (a+bi) pairs and small integers. The next page begins a sum over Gaussian-integer points x+iy in a region (Delta), with a floor-type bracket [ (1+i)(x+iy)(A+iB)/(a+ib) ] = alpha + i*l and a sum of squares of the resulting parts. This page looks like the algebraic bookkeeping for a reciprocity-type lattice-point sum of the kind used for Gauss's biquadratic (quartic) reciprocity work, evaluated by a continued-fraction style chain.

(1) Top block: a five-line alternating-sign sum with weights 1/4. Line k has the form +/- (1/4)(X - x)(Y - g*X' - Z + 2g) with consecutive letters (A,B,C,D,E,F,G) and the corresponding lowercase letters (a,b,c,d,e,f,g), with Gothic b, gamma, delta, epsilon, phi as additional multipliers (apparently small integer partial quotients of a chain, since the lower-right table lists values 2,1,2,8?,4 for them and 1/2 for the first). Signs alternate +,-,+,-,+. Below it is the grouped form (1/4)(b'B - gamma C + delta D - eps E + phi F) + (1/4)(AB - BC + 2CD - 2DE + 2EF - FG), which seems to be the result of expanding the products and collecting the terms that do not involve the lowercase letters.

(2) Middle block: the telescoping pieces -a/4 + b/4, -f/4 (+g/4), -bA/4 + aB/4, -gF/4 + fG/4 are boundary terms of the chain. Then the column AB-BC, -BC+CD, +CD-DE, -DE+EF, +EF-FG is the term by term listing of products of adjacent capital letters; adding these five rows gives AB - 2BC + 2CD - 2DE + 2EF - FG. The page's collected line (item 1) shows a single BC in the transcription, so either the image has a coefficient I cannot read or there is a slip; I flag this as unclear. Next to it are the mixed terms bA/4 + bC, b'B - cD, -dC + dE, +eD - eF, -fE + fG, and a second line 1/2 - b'b + gamma c - delta d + eps e - phi f.

(3) A small stack of signed lowercase terms (-a+c, +b-d, -c+e, +d-f, -e-g) is the same pattern of alternating differences with step 2, probably the linear terms of the same sum.

(4) Numerical evaluation on the right: a=379, b=107, c=70, d=31, e=4, f=1, g=0; capitals A=1, B=1, C=0, D=1, E=0, F=1, G=0; multipliers 1/2, 2, 1, 2, 8, 4 for the Gothic letters; n=6. Partial results written below: +9/4, +1/4, -138, -1/2 and +69. These look like the evaluated pieces of the formula with the total about -138 + 69 = -69 plus small fractions. I cannot reliably connect the list to the symbolic block, since a..g (379, 107, 70, 31, 4, 1, 0) do not form an obvious Euclidean remainder sequence. Bottom-left: a 0/1 pattern (1 0 1 1 0; 1 1 1 0) of unclear meaning, perhaps a parity check.

So the page is a worked evaluation of a six-step alternating continued-fraction sum with explicit numerical data, apparently a Dedekind-sum or lattice-point-count reciprocity formula for Gaussian integers. I could not recover the exact definition of the quantities, so I do not claim more.
